If Δ < 0, there are two complex roots. Finally, use the quadratic formula (x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / 2a) to find the roots.

To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function (f'(x)). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x (f'(x) = 0). The solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. Next, find the corresponding y-coordinates by substituting the x-values back into the original function (y = f(x)). Finally, to determine the nature of the stationary points, find the second derivative (f''(x)) and evaluate it at the stationary points. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
